subject: general
question: Pipe A is 3 times faster than pipe B. Both pipes together fill a tank in 36 min. How much time will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of efficiency **A : B = 3 : 1**

Total efficiency = **3 + 1 = 4 units/min**

Total work = **Total efficiency × Total time = 4 × 36 = 144 units**

Time taken by A alone = **Total work ÷ Efficiency of A = 144 ÷ 3 = 48 min**

**∴ The correct answer is 48 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Efficiency of Pipe A is 3 times that of Pipe B. Time taken together = 36 min.

**Formula Used:** Work = Efficiency × Time; Time = Work ÷ Efficiency

 **Pipe**
 **Efficiency (units/min)**
 **Total Work**
 **Time (min)**

 **Pipe A**
 3
 144
 144 ÷ 3 = 48

 **Pipe B**
 1
 144 ÷ 1 = 144

⇒ Let the efficiency of **Pipe B** be 1 unit/min.

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 3 × 1 = 3 units/min.

⇒ Combined efficiency of (A + B) = 3 + 1 = 4 units/min.

⇒ Total capacity of the tank = 4 units/min × 36 min = 144 units.

⇒ Time taken by Pipe A alone = 144 units ÷ 3 units/min = 48 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

The time taken to complete a work is **inversely proportional** to the efficiency. If Pipe A is 3 times faster than Pipe B, the ratio of time taken is 1 : 3.

Pipes and Cisterns Rule

If two pipes A and B fill a tank in x and y minutes respectively, then together they fill it in **(x × y) ÷ (x + y)** minutes.

Inlet and Outlet Concept

Inlet pipes carry **positive** efficiency, while outlet (leak) pipes carry **negative** efficiency when calculating total work per unit time.</p
